title: Warehouse events arrive late
briefing: Warehouse dispatch state is taking longer to update. Use queue and routing records to narrow the backlog.

actions.label: Compare lag by consumer partition
actions.criteria: Use when lag is elevated but it is unclear whether it affects all consumers or a subset of partitions.
actions.instructions: Compare lag, throughput, and consumer assignment across warehouse event partitions.

actions.label: Inspect routing-key skew
actions.criteria: Use when unrelated traffic is concentrated on one partition because a common or missing key collapses the distribution.
actions.instructions: Compare routing key frequencies and their partition assignments for affected event producers.

actions.label: Inspect consumer checkpoint delays
actions.criteria: Use when events are consumed but offset commits are failing or delayed across partitions.
actions.instructions: Compare processing completions with offset commit outcomes and checkpoint timestamps.

fallback: Collect a per-partition lag snapshot and one affected event with its routing key and offset.

events.text: Dispatch update age exceeded six minutes and the broker reports increased consumer lag. No partition breakdown is attached.
Lag rose on partition 7 while partitions 1 through 6 and 8 through 12 stayed close to their baseline.
Warehouse event publishers route by warehouse ID. An empty warehouse ID is replaced with default-v2, which the broker hashes to partition 7.
Of 20,000 messages recently routed to partition 7, 19,600 carried key=default-v2. Offset commits for partition 7 continued to succeed.

debrief.summary: One producer emitted dispatch events without warehouse IDs. The common fallback key sent almost all of them to the same partition.
lessons: A lagging partition is compatible with successful consumer checkpoints.
Join routing policy with observed key frequencies to distinguish assignment skew from consumer stalls.
